s.t: The studio was full of roses, and the door was open to the garden.
s.fr: L’atelier était rempli de roses, et la porte grande ouverte donnait sur le jardin.

s.t: Lord Henry Wotton sat and smoked, and he looked at the picture that stood in the middle of the room.
s.fr: Lord Henry Wotton, assis, fumait en contemplant le portrait qui trônait au milieu de la pièce.

s.t: It was a picture of a young man, and the young man was more beautiful than any man that Lord Henry had ever seen.
s.fr: C’était le portrait d’un jeune homme, et ce jeune homme était plus beau qu’aucun de ceux que lord Henry avait jamais vus.

s.t: Basil Hallward stood in front of it and did not look at his friend.
s.fr: Basil Hallward se tenait devant la toile sans regarder son ami.

s.t: "It is the best picture that you have ever painted, Basil," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « C’est ce que vous avez peint de mieux, Basil, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "You must send it to the gallery this year."
s.fr: « Il faut l’exposer cette année. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry Wotton sits in Basil Hallward's studio and looks at a picture of an extremely beautiful young man. He tells Basil it is his best work and that he should send it to the gallery.

s.t: "No, I will not send it anywhere," Basil said.
s.fr: « Non, je ne l’exposerai nulle part, » répondit Basil.

s.t: "I have put too much of myself into this picture."
s.fr: « J’ai mis trop de moi-même dans ce portrait. »

s.t: Lord Henry laughed.
s.fr: Lord Henry éclata de rire.

s.t: "I did not know that you were so vain, Basil," he said.
s.fr: « Je ne vous savais pas si vaniteux, Basil, » dit-il.

s.t: "You are a large plain man with dark hair, and this boy is young and beautiful."
s.fr: « Vous êtes un grand gaillard aux cheveux noirs, sans aucune beauté, et ce garçon est jeune et beau. »

s.t: "I am not vain," Basil said, "and I will tell you why I will not show the picture."
s.fr: « Je ne suis pas vaniteux, dit Basil, et je vais vous dire pourquoi je n’exposerai pas ce portrait. »

paras.summary: Basil says he will not show the picture because he has put too much of himself into it. Lord Henry laughs and calls him vain, and Basil says he will explain.

s.t: "Every picture that a man paints is a picture of the painter."
s.fr: « Tout portrait qu’un homme peint est le portrait du peintre. »

s.t: "It is not a picture of the person who sits for it."
s.fr: « Ce n’est pas le portrait de celui qui pose. »

s.t: "The person who sits is only the reason for the picture, and the painter puts himself on the canvas."
s.fr: « Le modèle n’est que le prétexte du portrait, et c’est lui-même que le peintre met sur la toile. »

s.t: "I am afraid that men will see my secret in this picture, and so I will not show it."
s.fr: « Je crains qu’on ne découvre mon secret dans ce portrait, et c’est pourquoi je ne l’exposerai pas. »

s.t: Lord Henry laughed again and asked, "What is the secret?"
s.fr: Lord Henry rit de nouveau et demanda : « Et quel est ce secret ? »

paras.summary: Basil says every painting shows the painter rather than the sitter, and he fears people will see his secret in this one. Lord Henry laughs and asks what the secret is.

s.t: "Who is the young man, and why do you care so much about him?" Lord Henry asked.
s.fr: « Qui est ce jeune homme, et pourquoi tenez-vous tant à lui ? » demanda lord Henry.

s.t: "His name is Dorian Gray," Basil said.
s.fr: « Il s’appelle Dorian Gray, » dit Basil.

s.t: "I have never heard that name," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Je n’ai jamais entendu ce nom, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "No one has heard it yet," Basil said, "but he is the most important thing in my life."
s.fr: « Personne ne le connaît encore, dit Basil, mais il est ce qui compte le plus dans ma vie. »

s.t: "Since I met him, I have painted better than I ever painted before."
s.fr: « Depuis que je l’ai rencontré, je peins mieux que je n’ai jamais peint. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry asks who the young man is. Basil says his name is Dorian Gray, no one knows him yet, and since meeting him Basil has painted better than ever.

s.t: "I must meet him, Basil," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Il faut que je fasse sa connaissance, Basil, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "No, you must not," Basil said.
s.fr: « Non, surtout pas, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You talk well, and you like to change the thoughts of other men, and I do not want you to change him."
s.fr: « Vous parlez bien, vous aimez changer la façon de penser des autres, et je ne veux pas que vous le changiez. »

s.t: "He is young, and I want him to stay as he is."
s.fr: « Il est jeune, et je veux qu’il reste tel qu’il est. »

s.t: Lord Henry smiled and did not say more.
s.fr: Lord Henry sourit et n’ajouta rien.

paras.summary: Lord Henry says he must meet Dorian, but Basil refuses, because Lord Henry likes to change other men's thoughts and Basil wants Dorian to stay as he is. Lord Henry only smiles.

s.t: "Tell me how you met him," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Racontez-moi comment vous l’avez connu, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: Basil looked at the picture for a time, and then he spoke.
s.fr: Basil contempla un moment le portrait, puis il prit la parole.

s.t: "I was at a party at the house of Lady Brandon, and I stood in the room for a time."
s.fr: « J’étais à une soirée chez lady Brandon, et je me tenais depuis un moment dans le salon. »

s.t: "I felt that someone was looking at me, and I turned, and I saw Dorian Gray."
s.fr: « J’ai senti qu’on me regardait, je me suis retourné, et j’ai vu Dorian Gray. »

s.t: "Dorian looked at me, and I was afraid, for I knew that he could take my whole life."
s.fr: « Dorian m’a regardé, et j’ai eu peur, car je savais qu’il pouvait s’emparer de ma vie tout entière. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry asks how Basil met Dorian. Basil says he was at a party at Lady Brandon's and felt someone looking at him. He turned and saw Dorian Gray, and he was afraid.

s.t: "I turned to go, but Lady Brandon stopped me and said that I must meet a young man."
s.fr: « Je me dirigeais vers la porte, mais lady Brandon m’a retenu en disant qu’il fallait absolument que je fasse la connaissance d’un jeune homme. »

s.t: "She took me to Dorian, and we spoke."
s.fr: « Elle m’a conduit jusqu’à Dorian, et nous avons parlé. »

s.t: "I have seen him every day since, and I paint nothing but him."
s.fr: « Depuis, je le vois tous les jours, et je ne peins plus que lui. »

s.t: "He is all my art now."
s.fr: « Mon art tout entier, c’est lui désormais. »

s.t: "In every picture that I paint, I see his face, and I have never seen anything so beautiful."
s.fr: « Dans chaque toile que je peins, je vois son visage, et je n’ai jamais rien vu d’aussi beau. »

paras.summary: Basil says Lady Brandon stopped him and introduced them. Since then he sees Dorian every day and paints nothing else, and he sees Dorian's face in every picture.

s.t: "That is why I will not show this picture, for men would see how much I love him."
s.fr: « Voilà pourquoi je n’exposerai pas ce portrait : on verrait à quel point je l’aime. »

s.t: Lord Henry looked at Basil for a time and said nothing.
s.fr: Lord Henry observa Basil un moment sans rien dire.

s.t: A servant came into the studio and said, "Dorian Gray has come, sir."
s.fr: Un domestique entra dans l’atelier et annonça : « M. Dorian Gray est arrivé, monsieur. »

s.t: "You must introduce me to him," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Il faut me présenter, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "I will," Basil said, "but do not spoil him, Harry, for he is the best thing in my life."
s.fr: « Soit, dit Basil, mais ne me le gâtez pas, Harry, car il est ce que j’ai de plus précieux au monde. »

paras.summary: Basil says he will not show the picture because men would see how much he loves Dorian. A servant announces Dorian, and Lord Henry asks to be introduced. Basil agrees but asks him not to spoil Dorian.

s.t: Basil went to the door, and Dorian came into the studio.
s.fr: Basil alla ouvrir, et Dorian entra dans l’atelier.

s.t: He was young and beautiful, and his face was honest.
s.fr: Il était jeune et beau, et son visage respirait la franchise.

s.t: "I am late, Basil," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Je suis en retard, Basil, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "This is Lord Henry Wotton, and he has been looking at your picture," Basil said.
s.fr: « Je vous présente lord Henry Wotton, qui contemplait votre portrait, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You must not listen to him."
s.fr: « Ne l’écoutez surtout pas. »

s.t: Dorian laughed and said, "I am not afraid of Lord Henry."
s.fr: Dorian se mit à rire et répondit : « Lord Henry ne me fait pas peur. »

paras.summary: Dorian comes into the studio, young and beautiful, and says he is late. Basil introduces Lord Henry and tells Dorian not to listen to him, but Dorian laughs and says he is not afraid of him.

s.t: Lord Henry held out his hand and said, "I know your name, and I am glad to meet you."
s.fr: Lord Henry lui tendit la main et dit : « Je connais votre nom, et je suis ravi de faire votre connaissance. »

s.t: "Basil has told me about you, and I have looked at your picture for a long time."
s.fr: « Basil m’a parlé de vous, et j’ai longuement regardé votre portrait. »

s.t: "I have not seen a picture so beautiful, and I have not seen a young man so beautiful."
s.fr: « Jamais je n’ai vu un aussi beau portrait, ni un aussi beau jeune homme. »

s.t: Dorian looked at the picture and then at Lord Henry, and he smiled.
s.fr: Dorian regarda le portrait, puis lord Henry, et il sourit.

paras.summary: Lord Henry greets Dorian warmly and says he has looked at the picture for a long time and never saw a young man so beautiful. Dorian looks at the picture and at Lord Henry and smiles.

s.t: "Harry, I want to finish this picture, and you must go," Basil said.
s.fr: « Harry, je veux achever ce portrait, et il faut que vous partiez, » dit Basil.

s.t: Lord Henry looked at Dorian and asked, "Do you want me to go?"
s.fr: Lord Henry regarda Dorian et demanda : « Voulez-vous que je parte ? »

s.t: "No, do not go," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Non, ne partez pas, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "Basil, I like to listen to Lord Henry, and I want him to stay."
s.fr: « Basil, j’aime écouter lord Henry, et je veux qu’il reste. »

s.t: Basil said nothing for a time, and then he painted again.
s.fr: Basil garda le silence un moment, puis se remit à peindre.

paras.summary: Basil asks Lord Henry to leave so he can finish the picture, but Dorian asks him to stay. Basil says nothing and paints again.

s.t: Dorian stood in front of Basil, and Lord Henry sat and looked at him.
s.fr: Dorian posait devant Basil, et lord Henry, assis, l’observait.

s.t: "You have youth, and you have beauty, and they are the best things that a man can have," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Vous avez la jeunesse et la beauté, ce qu’un homme peut posséder de plus précieux, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "You have a beautiful face, and everyone will love you for it, but only while you are young."
s.fr: « Vous avez un visage magnifique, et c’est pour lui que tout le monde vous aimera, mais seulement tant que vous serez jeune. »

s.t: "In a few years you will be old, and your face will not be beautiful."
s.fr: « Dans quelques années, vous serez vieux, et votre visage aura perdu sa beauté. »

s.t: "After that you will know that your youth is gone."
s.fr: « Alors vous comprendrez que votre jeunesse s’est enfuie. »

paras.summary: Dorian stands in front of Basil while Lord Henry says that youth and beauty are the best things a man can have. Everyone will love Dorian's face while he is young, he says, but in a few years he will be old.

s.t: "Youth will not come again," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « La jeunesse ne revient pas, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "So you must live now, for you are young."
s.fr: « Il faut donc vivre maintenant, pendant que vous êtes jeune. »

s.t: "Beauty is better than any thought, for beauty needs no reason."
s.fr: « La beauté vaut mieux que toute pensée, car elle se passe de raisons. »

s.t: "Do not listen to men who tell you what to think."
s.fr: « N’écoutez pas ceux qui veulent vous dicter ce qu’il faut penser. »

s.t: "Live, and do what you want to do, for you are young."
s.fr: « Vivez, faites ce qui vous plaît, puisque vous êtes jeune. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry says youth does not come again, so Dorian must live now. Beauty needs no reason, he says, and Dorian should not listen to men who tell him what to think.

s.t: Dorian listened, and his face was strange.
s.fr: Dorian écoutait, et son visage avait pris un air étrange.

s.t: He had never heard these words, and he did not know what to say.
s.fr: Jamais il n’avait entendu de telles paroles, et il ne savait que répondre.

s.t: Basil painted on, and he did not look up.
s.fr: Basil continuait de peindre sans lever les yeux.

s.t: "Stop, Harry," Basil said.
s.fr: « Assez, Harry, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You are confusing Dorian, and I cannot paint his face."
s.fr: « Vous troublez Dorian, et je n’arrive plus à peindre son visage. »

paras.summary: Dorian listens with a strange face, for he has never heard such words. Basil tells Lord Henry to stop because he is confusing Dorian.

s.t: Lord Henry smiled and said, "I have said only what I think."
s.fr: Lord Henry sourit et répondit : « Je n’ai dit que ce que je pense. »

s.t: "You are young, Dorian, and you must think about what I said."
s.fr: « Vous êtes jeune, Dorian, et vous devez réfléchir à ce que je vous ai dit. »

s.t: Dorian did not speak, and he looked at the roses in the garden.
s.fr: Dorian ne dit rien et regarda les roses du jardin.

s.t: "They are beautiful, and they will not last," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Elles sont belles, et elles ne dureront pas, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: Dorian turned to him and asked, "Is it true that I will not be beautiful for long?"
s.fr: Dorian se tourna vers lui et demanda : « Est-il vrai que je ne resterai pas beau longtemps ? »

s.t: "It is true," Lord Henry said, "and that is why you must live now."
s.fr: « C’est vrai, dit lord Henry, et voilà pourquoi vous devez vivre maintenant. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry says he has said only what he thinks. Dorian looks at the roses, which Lord Henry says will not last, and asks if he will not be beautiful for long. Lord Henry says it is true and tells him to live now.

s.t: At last Basil put down his brush and said, "It is finished."
s.fr: Enfin Basil posa son pinceau et déclara : « Il est achevé. »

s.t: Lord Henry looked at the picture and said, "It is the best picture that you have ever painted."
s.fr: Lord Henry examina le portrait et dit : « C’est ce que vous avez peint de mieux. »

s.t: "Dorian, come and look at it," Basil said.
s.fr: « Dorian, venez le voir, » dit Basil.

s.t: Dorian came and stood in front of the picture, and he did not speak for a long time.
s.fr: Dorian s’approcha et se plaça devant le portrait, et il resta longtemps sans parler.

s.t: He saw his own face for the first time, and it was more beautiful than he had known.
s.fr: Il voyait pour la première fois son propre visage, et ce visage était plus beau qu’il ne l’avait jamais imaginé.

paras.summary: Basil puts down his brush and says the picture is finished, and Lord Henry says it is his best. Dorian looks at it for a long time and sees his own face for the first time.

s.t: Dorian's eyes were wet, and he said, "It is beautiful, but I will change, and the picture will not change."
s.fr: Dorian avait les yeux humides, et il dit : « Il est beau, mais moi, je vais changer, et le portrait, lui, ne changera pas. »

s.t: "I will be old, and my face will not be beautiful, but the picture will always be young."
s.fr: « Je vieillirai, mon visage perdra sa beauté, mais le portrait restera toujours jeune. »

s.t: "I wish that I could always be young, and that the picture could grow old in my place."
s.fr: « Si seulement je pouvais rester toujours jeune, et si le portrait pouvait vieillir à ma place ! »

s.t: "I would give my soul for that."
s.fr: « Pour cela, je donnerais mon âme. »

paras.summary: Dorian's eyes are wet as he says the picture will stay young while he grows old. He wishes he could stay young while the picture grows old, and says he would give his soul for that.

s.t: Basil looked at him and asked, "Dorian, what are you saying?"
s.fr: Basil le regarda et demanda : « Dorian, que dites-vous là ? »

s.t: "Harry has told you that you will be old, and now you are sad."
s.fr: « Harry vous a dit que vous vieilliriez, et vous voilà triste. »

s.t: "I am jealous of the picture, for you like it better than you like me," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Je suis jaloux du portrait, car vous l’aimez plus que moi, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "You are jealous of a picture, and that is not right," Basil said.
s.fr: « Être jaloux d’un portrait, ce n’est pas bien, » dit Basil.

s.t: Dorian saw a knife on the table, and he took it in his hand.
s.fr: Dorian aperçut un couteau sur la table et s’en saisit.

paras.summary: Basil says Dorian is sad because Harry told him he would be old. Dorian says he is jealous because Basil likes the picture better than him, and he picks up a knife from the table.

s.t: "I will cut the picture," Dorian said, "for I do not want it to be there when I am old."
s.fr: « Je vais lacérer ce portrait, dit Dorian, car je ne veux pas qu’il soit encore là quand je serai vieux. »

s.t: "Do not do it, Dorian!" Basil cried, and he took the knife from Dorian's hand.
s.fr: « Ne faites pas cela, Dorian ! » s’écria Basil, et il lui arracha le couteau des mains.

s.t: "That would be murder, for the picture is a part of my life."
s.fr: « Ce serait un meurtre, car ce portrait fait partie de ma vie. »

s.t: "I like it better than any picture that I have made, and I like you better than the picture."
s.fr: « Je l’aime plus que tout ce que j’ai jamais peint, et je vous aime plus encore que lui. »

paras.summary: Dorian says he will cut the picture, but Basil takes the knife, saying it would be murder and that he likes Dorian better.

s.t: "I will give you the picture, Dorian," Basil said.
s.fr: « Je vous donne ce portrait, Dorian, » dit Basil.

s.t: "It is yours, and I made it for you."
s.fr: « Il est à vous, et je l’ai peint pour vous. »

s.t: Lord Henry smiled and said, "It is a good thing to have a picture of yourself."
s.fr: Lord Henry sourit et dit : « C’est une bonne chose que d’avoir son propre portrait. »

s.t: "Come with me, Dorian, and we will eat dinner and go to the opera."
s.fr: « Venez avec moi, Dorian, nous dînerons ensemble, puis nous irons à l’opéra. »

s.t: Dorian looked at the picture once more and said, "I will go with you."
s.fr: Dorian jeta un dernier regard au portrait et répondit : « Je viens avec vous. »

paras.summary: Basil gives the picture to Dorian. Lord Henry asks him to come to dinner and the opera, and Dorian agrees.

s.t: The next day Lord Henry went to see his uncle, Lord Fermor, who was an old man and knew everyone.
s.fr: Le lendemain, lord Henry alla rendre visite à son oncle, lord Fermor, un vieillard qui connaissait tout le monde.

s.t: "Uncle George, who is Dorian Gray?" Lord Henry asked.
s.fr: « Oncle George, qui est Dorian Gray ? » demanda lord Henry.

s.t: "He is the grandson of old Lord Kelso," the old man said.
s.fr: « C’est le petit-fils du vieux lord Kelso, » répondit le vieillard.

s.t: "His mother was Margaret Devereux, and she was the most beautiful girl that I have ever seen."
s.fr: « Sa mère était Margaret Devereux, la plus belle jeune fille que j’aie jamais vue. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry visits his old uncle, Lord Fermor, and asks who Dorian is. His uncle says Dorian is the grandson of Lord Kelso and that his mother was the beautiful Margaret Devereux.

s.t: "She ran away with a poor young soldier, and her father did not like it."
s.fr: « Elle s’est enfuie avec un jeune soldat sans le sou, et son père l’a très mal pris. »

s.t: "The soldier was killed a year later, and Margaret died soon after."
s.fr: « Le soldat a été tué un an plus tard, et Margaret est morte peu après. »

s.t: "The boy grew up with his grandfather, and he has no one now."
s.fr: « Le garçon a été élevé par son grand-père, et il n’a plus personne aujourd’hui. »

s.t: "He has a great deal of money, for old Kelso left it all to him."
s.fr: « Il a énormément d’argent, car le vieux Kelso lui a tout laissé. »

paras.summary: Margaret ran away with a poor soldier, who was killed a year later, and she died soon after. Dorian grew up with his grandfather and now has a great deal of money.

s.t: Lord Henry thanked his uncle and went out into the street.
s.fr: Lord Henry remercia son oncle et sortit dans la rue.

s.t: He thought about Dorian, who was young and beautiful and rich and alone.
s.fr: Il songeait à Dorian, jeune, beau, riche et seul au monde.

s.t: "It would be strange to make such a young man think as I think," he said to himself.
s.fr: « Ce serait étrange d’amener un pareil jeune homme à penser comme moi, » se dit-il.

s.t: "He would do what I say, and he would not know why."
s.fr: « Il ferait tout ce que je dirais, sans même savoir pourquoi. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry thanks his uncle and walks into the street, thinking of Dorian as young, beautiful, rich, and alone. He thinks it would be strange to make Dorian think as he does.

s.t: That night Lord Henry ate dinner at the house of his aunt Agatha, and Dorian was there.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, lord Henry dîna chez sa tante Agatha, et Dorian était parmi les convives.

s.t: Dorian spoke to everyone at the table, and everyone liked him.
s.fr: Dorian bavarda avec tous les convives, et tous le trouvèrent charmant.

s.t: After dinner Dorian sat by Lord Henry and said, "I have thought about what you told me, Harry."
s.fr: Après le dîner, Dorian vint s’asseoir auprès de lord Henry et lui dit : « J’ai réfléchi à ce que vous m’avez dit, Harry. »

s.t: "You told me to live, and I want to live, but I do not know how."
s.fr: « Vous m’avez dit de vivre, et je veux vivre, mais je ne sais pas comment. »

s.t: "I will show you," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Je vous montrerai, » dit lord Henry.

paras.summary: That night Lord Henry dines at his aunt Agatha's house, where Dorian is liked by everyone. After dinner Dorian says he wants to live as Lord Henry told him but does not know how, and Lord Henry says he will show him.

s.t: "You are young, and you are beautiful, and you have money, and you can do what you want."
s.fr: « Vous êtes jeune, vous êtes beau, vous avez de l’argent, et vous pouvez faire tout ce qui vous plaît. »

s.t: "Come with me to the theatres and the clubs, and I will teach you to see what is beautiful."
s.fr: « Suivez-moi dans les théâtres et dans les cercles, et je vous apprendrai à voir ce qui est beau. »

s.t: "You must not think about what men say, for men say what they do not think."
s.fr: « Ne vous souciez pas de ce que disent les gens, car les gens disent ce qu’ils ne pensent pas. »

s.t: "Do you want to come?"
s.fr: « Voulez-vous venir ? »

s.t: "I do," Dorian said, and he smiled.
s.fr: « Je le veux, » dit Dorian, et il sourit.

paras.summary: Lord Henry tells Dorian he is young, beautiful, and rich and offers to teach him to see what is beautiful in the theatres and clubs. Dorian says he wants to come.

s.t: Three weeks later Dorian came to lunch at the house of Lord Henry, and his face was bright.
s.fr: Trois semaines plus tard, Dorian vint déjeuner chez lord Henry, le visage radieux.

s.t: "Harry, I am in love," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Harry, je suis amoureux, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "I have found a girl, and her name is Sibyl Vane."
s.fr: « J’ai découvert une jeune fille, et elle s’appelle Sibyl Vane. »

s.t: "She is an actress, and she plays in a small theatre in a poor part of London."
s.fr: « Elle est actrice, et elle joue dans un petit théâtre d’un quartier pauvre de Londres. »

s.t: "I went in one night because I saw a picture on the wall, and the theatre was dirty."
s.fr: « Un soir, j’y suis entré à cause d’une affiche collée au mur, et le théâtre était crasseux. »

paras.summary: Three weeks later Dorian comes to lunch at Lord Henry's house and says he is in love with an actress named Sibyl Vane, who plays in a small theatre in a poor part of London.

s.t: "The people in the theatre were rough, and the play was bad, and I wanted to go home."
s.fr: « Le public était grossier, la pièce était mauvaise, et j’avais envie de rentrer chez moi. »

s.t: "Then Sibyl came on, and she was the most beautiful girl that I have ever seen."
s.fr: « Puis Sibyl est entrée en scène, et c’était la plus belle jeune fille que j’aie jamais vue. »

s.t: "She is only seventeen, and she has a small face and a great deal of brown hair."
s.fr: « Elle n’a que dix-sept ans, un petit visage et une abondante chevelure brune. »

s.t: "She played Juliet, and her voice was the most beautiful voice that I have ever heard."
s.fr: « Elle jouait Juliette, et sa voix était la plus belle que j’aie jamais entendue. »

s.t: "I have been to see her every night for a week, and each night she plays a different girl."
s.fr: « Voilà une semaine que je vais la voir tous les soirs, et chaque soir elle incarne une autre jeune fille. »

paras.summary: The audience is rough and the play is bad, but when Sibyl comes on she is the most beautiful girl Dorian has seen. She is seventeen, and he has watched her every night for a week.

s.t: "One night she is Rosalind, and the next night she is Juliet, and I love them all," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Un soir elle est Rosalinde, le lendemain Juliette, et je les aime toutes, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "I spoke to her after the play, and I asked her to marry me, and she said yes."
s.fr: « Je lui ai parlé après la représentation, je l’ai demandée en mariage, et elle a dit oui. »

s.t: "I love her, Harry, and I am going to marry her."
s.fr: « Je l’aime, Harry, et je vais l’épouser. »

s.t: "You are going to marry an actress?" Lord Henry asked.
s.fr: « Vous allez épouser une actrice ? » demanda lord Henry.

s.t: "You are young, and you do not know that you will be tired of her."
s.fr: « Vous êtes jeune, et vous ignorez qu’elle finira par vous lasser. »

s.t: "I will never be tired of her," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Jamais elle ne me lassera, » dit Dorian.

paras.summary: Dorian says he loves her in every part she plays and has asked her to marry him and she said yes. Lord Henry says Dorian will grow tired of her, but Dorian says he never will.

s.t: "Basil and you must come to the theatre and see her," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Basil et vous, il faut que vous veniez la voir au théâtre, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "You will see that she is not like other girls."
s.fr: « Vous verrez qu’elle ne ressemble à aucune autre. »

s.t: "Come to the theatre tomorrow night, and bring Basil."
s.fr: « Venez au théâtre demain soir, et amenez Basil. »

s.t: "I will bring him, for I want to see the girl who has done this to you," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Je l’amènerai, car je tiens à voir la jeune fille qui vous a mis dans cet état, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: Dorian laughed and thanked him, and his face was bright again.
s.fr: Dorian rit et le remercia, et son visage s’illumina de nouveau.

paras.summary: Dorian asks Lord Henry to bring Basil to see Sibyl tomorrow night. Lord Henry agrees, for he wants to see the girl.

s.t: That evening Sibyl Vane sat in a small room with her mother and her brother James, and her eyes were bright.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, Sibyl Vane était assise dans une petite pièce avec sa mère et son frère James, et ses yeux brillaient.

s.t: "I am so happy," Sibyl said, "for I love him, and he loves me."
s.fr: « Je suis si heureuse, dit Sibyl, car je l’aime, et il m’aime. »

s.t: "Who is he?" James asked.
s.fr: « Qui est-ce ? » demanda James.

s.t: "I do not know his name, and I call him the Prince," Sibyl said.
s.fr: « Je ne connais pas son nom, et je l’appelle le Prince Charmant, » dit Sibyl.

s.t: "He comes to the theatre every night, and he is young and beautiful and rich."
s.fr: « Il vient au théâtre tous les soirs, et il est jeune, beau et riche. »

paras.summary: That evening Sibyl sits with her mother and brother James and says she loves a young, beautiful, rich man who comes to the theatre every night. She does not know his name and calls him the Prince.

s.t: "When I am on the stage, I know that he is there, and I act better than I have ever acted."
s.fr: « Quand je suis en scène, je sais qu’il est là, et je joue mieux que je n’ai jamais joué. »

s.t: James looked at Sibyl for a long time and said, "You are only seventeen, and you do not know men."
s.fr: James regarda longuement Sibyl et dit : « Tu n’as que dix-sept ans, et tu ne connais pas les hommes. »

s.t: "You do not know his name," James said, "and I do not like it."
s.fr: « Tu ne connais même pas son nom, dit James, et cela ne me plaît pas. »

s.t: "A man who does not tell his name is not an honest man."
s.fr: « Un homme qui cache son nom n’est pas un honnête homme. »

s.t: "He is a gentleman, James, and he will marry Sibyl," their mother said.
s.fr: « C’est un homme du monde, James, et il épousera Sibyl, » dit leur mère.

paras.summary: Sibyl says she acts better when he is there. James says she is only seventeen and does not know men, and that a man who does not tell his name is not honest, but their mother says he is a gentleman who will marry Sibyl.

s.t: "We have no money, and we owe money to the man of the theatre."
s.fr: « Nous n’avons pas d’argent, et nous devons de l’argent au directeur du théâtre. »

s.t: "If Sibyl marries a rich man, we will not be poor."
s.fr: « Si Sibyl épouse un homme riche, nous ne serons plus pauvres. »

s.t: "You think only about money, mother," Sibyl said.
s.fr: « Tu ne penses qu’à l’argent, maman, » dit Sibyl.

s.t: "I do not think about money, for I love him."
s.fr: « Moi, je ne pense pas à l’argent, car je l’aime. »

s.t: "I am going away tomorrow, Sibyl, and I will be at sea for many years," James said.
s.fr: « Je pars demain, Sibyl, et je serai en mer pendant de longues années, » dit James.

s.t: "I am going to Australia, and I want you to be safe."
s.fr: « Je pars pour l’Australie, et je veux te savoir à l’abri. »

paras.summary: Their mother says they owe money and that a rich husband would help them. Sibyl says her mother thinks only about money. James says he is going to Australia tomorrow for many years and wants Sibyl to be safe.

s.t: "I will be safe, James," Sibyl said, and she kissed him.
s.fr: « Il ne m’arrivera rien, James, » dit Sibyl, et elle l’embrassa.

s.t: "Write to me from Australia."
s.fr: « Écris-moi d’Australie. »

s.t: Later James spoke to his mother alone.
s.fr: Plus tard, James prit sa mère à part.

s.t: "Take care of Sibyl, mother, for I do not trust this man," James said.
s.fr: « Veille sur Sibyl, maman, car je n’ai pas confiance en cet homme, » dit James.

s.t: "If he does wrong to my sister, I will find him and I will kill him."
s.fr: « S’il fait du mal à ma sœur, je le retrouverai et je le tuerai. »

s.t: His mother cried out and said, "James, you speak like a bad man in a play."
s.fr: Sa mère poussa un cri et dit : « James, tu parles comme un traître de mélodrame. »

s.t: "I speak as I feel, mother," James said, and he went out of the room.
s.fr: « Je dis ce que je ressens, maman, » dit James, et il quitta la pièce.

paras.summary: Sibyl says she will be safe. Later James tells his mother to take care of Sibyl and says he will find and kill the man if he wrongs her. His mother says he speaks like a man in a play, and James leaves.

s.t: The next night Dorian, Basil, and Lord Henry sat in a box at the small theatre.
s.fr: Le lendemain soir, Dorian, Basil et lord Henry prirent place dans une loge du petit théâtre.

s.t: The theatre was dirty, and the people in it were rough.
s.fr: Le théâtre était crasseux, et le public grossier.

s.t: "This is a strange place for a young man to find his love," Basil said.
s.fr: « Voilà un étrange endroit pour qu’un jeune homme y trouve l’amour, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You will not think so when you see her," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Vous changerez d’avis quand vous la verrez, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "Sibyl Vane is the best actress that I have ever seen, and I will marry her."
s.fr: « Sibyl Vane est la meilleure actrice que j’aie jamais vue, et je l’épouserai. »

paras.summary: The next night Dorian, Basil, and Lord Henry sit in a box at the small theatre. Basil says it is a strange place to find love, and Dorian says Sibyl is the best actress he has seen.

s.t: Sibyl came on the stage as Juliet, and she was as beautiful as Dorian had said.
s.fr: Sibyl entra en scène dans le rôle de Juliette, et elle était aussi belle que Dorian l’avait dit.

s.t: But her voice was not beautiful, and her words were bad.
s.fr: Mais sa voix n’avait rien de beau, et elle disait son texte fort mal.

s.t: She stood on the stage, and she did not know what to say.
s.fr: Elle restait plantée sur la scène sans savoir que dire.

s.t: Dorian looked at her, and his face was strange.
s.fr: Dorian la regardait, et son visage avait pris un air étrange.

s.t: "She is beautiful, but she cannot act," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Elle est belle, mais elle ne sait pas jouer, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "She may be afraid because we are here," Basil said.
s.fr: « Peut-être notre présence l’intimide-t-elle, » dit Basil.

paras.summary: Sibyl comes on as Juliet, as beautiful as Dorian said, but her voice is not beautiful and her words are bad. Dorian looks strange, and Lord Henry says she cannot act, but Basil says she may be afraid.

s.t: The people in the theatre laughed, and they called out to her.
s.fr: Le public riait et l’apostrophait.

s.t: A rough man cried, "Go home, girl, and say your words better!"
s.fr: Un rustre cria : « Rentre chez toi, petite, et apprends à dire ton texte ! »

s.t: Sibyl did not hear them, and she went on.
s.fr: Sibyl ne les entendait pas, et elle continua.

s.t: Dorian could not look at her, and he did not speak.
s.fr: Dorian ne pouvait plus la regarder, et il ne disait rien.

s.t: "We must go, Dorian," Basil said.
s.fr: « Il faut partir, Dorian, » dit Basil.

s.t: "No, I will stay," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Non, je reste, » dit Dorian.

paras.summary: The people laugh, and a rough man tells Sibyl to go home. Dorian cannot look at her, and when Basil says they must go, he says he will stay.

s.t: "I told you that she was the best actress that I had ever seen," Dorian said in a low voice.
s.fr: « Je vous avais dit que c’était la meilleure actrice que j’aie jamais vue, » dit Dorian à voix basse.

s.t: "Now you think that I was wrong, and you are laughing at me."
s.fr: « Maintenant vous pensez que je me suis trompé, et vous vous moquez de moi. »

s.t: "We are not laughing at you," Basil said.
s.fr: « Nous ne nous moquons pas de vous, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You are young, and you love her, and that is not a bad thing."
s.fr: « Vous êtes jeune, vous l’aimez, et il n’y a là rien de mal. »

paras.summary: Dorian says they must think him wrong about Sibyl. Basil says they are not laughing at him and that loving her is not bad.

s.t: When the play was over, Lord Henry stood up and said, "She is bad, Dorian."
s.fr: Quand le rideau tomba, lord Henry se leva et dit : « Elle est mauvaise, Dorian. »

s.t: "You must not marry her, for she will never be a great actress."
s.fr: « Vous ne devez pas l’épouser, car elle ne sera jamais une grande actrice. »

s.t: "She is a beautiful girl, and that is all."
s.fr: « C’est une belle fille, voilà tout. »

s.t: "I am sorry, Dorian," Basil said, "for I did not know that she would be so bad."
s.fr: « Je suis désolé, Dorian, dit Basil, je ne pensais pas qu’elle serait si mauvaise. »

s.t: "Go and speak to her."
s.fr: « Allez lui parler. »

s.t: Dorian said nothing, and he went out of the box to find Sibyl.
s.fr: Dorian ne dit rien et quitta la loge pour aller retrouver Sibyl.

paras.summary: When the play is over, Lord Henry says Sibyl will never be a great actress and Dorian must not marry her. Basil tells Dorian to speak to her, and Dorian goes to find her.

s.t: Dorian found Sibyl in her small room behind the stage, and she ran to him.
s.fr: Dorian trouva Sibyl dans sa petite loge, derrière la scène, et elle courut vers lui.

s.t: "Prince, I was so bad tonight," Sibyl said, and her face was bright with joy.
s.fr: « Prince Charmant, j’ai été si mauvaise ce soir, » dit Sibyl, le visage rayonnant de joie.

s.t: "I have never acted so badly, but I am not sorry."
s.fr: « Je n’ai jamais si mal joué, mais je ne le regrette pas. »

s.t: "I do not understand you," Dorian said coldly.
s.fr: « Je ne vous comprends pas, » dit Dorian d’un ton glacial.

s.t: Sibyl took his hands and said, "Do you not see why I was bad?"
s.fr: Sibyl lui prit les mains et dit : « Ne voyez-vous pas pourquoi j’ai été mauvaise ? »

paras.summary: Dorian finds Sibyl behind the stage, and she runs to him and says she was bad tonight but is not sorry. Dorian coldly says he does not understand.

s.t: "I have always acted, and I thought that the stage was real," Sibyl said.
s.fr: « J’ai toujours joué, et je croyais que la scène était la vraie vie, » dit Sibyl.

s.t: "Before I met you, I loved the plays, and I thought that the people in them were true."
s.fr: « Avant de vous connaître, j’aimais les pièces, et je croyais que les personnages étaient de chair et de sang. »

s.t: "Tonight I saw that the stage is only paint, and that the people on it are only actors."
s.fr: « Ce soir, j’ai compris que la scène n’est que du carton peint, et que ceux qui y jouent ne sont que des comédiens. »

s.t: "Now I know what love is, and I cannot act love when I have love."
s.fr: « Maintenant je sais ce qu’est l’amour, et je ne peux pas jouer l’amour quand je l’éprouve. »

s.t: "I was bad because I love you, and I will never act well again."
s.fr: « J’ai été mauvaise parce que je vous aime, et je ne jouerai plus jamais bien. »

paras.summary: Sibyl says she once thought the stage was real. Tonight she saw it was only paint and now knows what love is, so she could not act it.

s.t: Dorian looked at her, and his face was hard.
s.fr: Dorian la regarda, et son visage était dur.

s.t: "You have spoiled my love," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Vous avez gâché mon amour, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "You have shown me that you are not the girl that I thought."
s.fr: « Vous m’avez montré que vous n’étiez pas celle que je croyais. »

s.t: "I loved you because you were a great actress, and now you are a bad actress."
s.fr: « Je vous aimais parce que vous étiez une grande actrice, et vous voilà devenue une piètre actrice. »

s.t: "I do not love you now, and I do not want to see you again."
s.fr: « Je ne vous aime plus, et je ne veux plus vous revoir. »

s.t: Sibyl fell on her knees and cried, but Dorian did not look at her.
s.fr: Sibyl tomba à genoux en sanglotant, mais Dorian ne la regarda pas.

paras.summary: Dorian says he loved her because she was a great actress and now she is bad, so he does not love her. Sibyl kneels and cries, but he does not look at her.

s.t: "Do not leave me, Prince, for I love you," Sibyl said.
s.fr: « Ne me quittez pas, Prince Charmant, car je vous aime, » dit Sibyl.

s.t: "I could not live if you left me."
s.fr: « Je ne pourrais pas vivre si vous me quittiez. »

s.t: "Say that you forgive me, and say that you will come tomorrow."
s.fr: « Dites que vous me pardonnez, et dites que vous reviendrez demain. »

s.t: "I do not care," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Peu m’importe, » dit Dorian.

paras.summary: Sibyl begs him not to leave and to forgive her, but Dorian says he does not care.

s.t: "You are only a girl, and you are not clever, and I was a fool to love you."
s.fr: « Vous n’êtes qu’une gamine sans esprit, et j’ai été fou de vous aimer. »

s.t: He walked out of the room and into the street, and he did not look back.
s.fr: Il sortit de la loge et gagna la rue sans se retourner.

s.t: The night was cold, and the street was empty.
s.fr: La nuit était froide, et la rue déserte.

s.t: Sibyl lay on the floor and cried until the theatre was empty.
s.fr: Sibyl resta étendue sur le plancher et pleura jusqu’à ce que le théâtre fût vide.

paras.summary: Dorian says she is not clever and that he was a fool to love her. He leaves, and Sibyl lies on the floor crying.

s.t: Dorian walked in the streets all night, and in the morning he went home.
s.fr: Dorian erra dans les rues toute la nuit, et au matin il rentra chez lui.

s.t: In his room the picture stood on the wall, and he looked at it.
s.fr: Dans sa chambre, le portrait était accroché au mur, et il le regarda.

s.t: The face in the picture was young, but the mouth was strange.
s.fr: Le visage du portrait était jeune, mais la bouche avait quelque chose d’étrange.

s.t: The mouth was cruel now, and it had not been cruel before.
s.fr: La bouche avait désormais un pli cruel qu’elle n’avait pas auparavant.

s.t: He told himself that the light was bad, and he looked at the picture again.
s.fr: Il se dit que la lumière le trompait, et il regarda de nouveau le portrait.

s.t: The change was still there.
s.fr: Le changement était toujours là.

paras.summary: Dorian walks all night and goes home in the morning to look at the picture. The face is young, but the mouth is strange and cruel, and it was not cruel before.

s.t: He thought of the wish that he had made in the studio, and he was afraid.
s.fr: Il se rappela le vœu qu’il avait formé dans l’atelier, et il eut peur.

s.t: "I wanted the picture to grow old, and I wanted to stay young," he said.
s.fr: « J’ai souhaité que le portrait vieillisse et que je reste jeune, » dit-il.

s.t: "Could it be true?"
s.fr: « Serait-ce vrai ? »

s.t: "No, it cannot be true, and I am tired," he said to himself.
s.fr: « Non, ce ne peut pas être vrai, je suis seulement fatigué, » se dit-il.

s.t: But the mouth in the picture was cruel, and he could not stop looking at it.
s.fr: Mais la bouche du portrait restait cruelle, et il ne pouvait en détacher les yeux.

paras.summary: Dorian remembers his wish and is afraid. He tells himself it cannot be true, but he cannot stop looking at the cruel mouth.

s.t: He thought of Sibyl, and he remembered her face when he left.
s.fr: Il pensa à Sibyl, et il revit son visage au moment où il l’avait quittée.

s.t: "I was cruel to Sibyl, and the picture shows it," Dorian said.
s.fr: « J’ai été cruel envers Sibyl, et le portrait le montre, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "I will go to her and ask her to forgive me, and I will marry her."
s.fr: « J’irai la trouver, je lui demanderai pardon, et je l’épouserai. »

s.t: "If I do good, the picture will change back, and it will be beautiful again."
s.fr: « Si je fais le bien, le portrait redeviendra comme avant, et il retrouvera sa beauté. »

s.t: He put a large screen in front of the picture, for he did not want to see it.
s.fr: Il plaça un grand paravent devant le portrait, car il ne voulait plus le voir.

s.t: He sat down and wrote a long letter to Sibyl, and he asked her to forgive him.
s.fr: Il s’assit et écrivit une longue lettre à Sibyl pour lui demander pardon.

paras.summary: Dorian says the picture shows his cruelty, and he resolves to ask Sibyl to forgive him and marry her, hoping the picture will change back. He puts a screen in front of it and writes Sibyl a long letter.

s.t: Later Lord Henry came into the room, and his face was strange.
s.fr: Plus tard, lord Henry entra dans la chambre, et son visage avait un air étrange.

s.t: "Dorian, I have come to tell you a sad thing," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Dorian, je viens vous annoncer une triste nouvelle, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "Sibyl Vane is dead."
s.fr: « Sibyl Vane est morte. »

s.t: "She took poison last night, and they found her in the morning."
s.fr: « Elle a avalé du poison hier soir, et on l’a trouvée ce matin. »

s.t: Dorian cried out, and he did not speak for a long time.
s.fr: Dorian poussa un cri, puis resta longtemps sans parler.

s.t: "Did she do it because of me?" Dorian asked.
s.fr: « Est-ce à cause de moi qu’elle a fait cela ? » demanda Dorian.

s.t: "I do not know," Lord Henry said, "but she was alone after you left."
s.fr: « Je l’ignore, dit lord Henry, mais elle était seule après votre départ. »

paras.summary: Later Lord Henry comes in with a strange face and says Sibyl Vane took poison last night and is dead. Dorian cries out and asks if she did it because of him, and Lord Henry says only that she was alone after Dorian left.

s.t: "She died because of me," Dorian said at last.
s.fr: « Elle est morte à cause de moi, » dit enfin Dorian.

s.t: "You are wrong, Dorian," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Vous vous trompez, Dorian, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "She took the poison herself, and you did not know that she would do it."
s.fr: « C’est elle qui a avalé ce poison, et vous ne pouviez pas savoir qu’elle le ferait. »

s.t: "You were cruel to her, but you did not want her to die."
s.fr: « Vous avez été cruel envers elle, mais vous ne vouliez pas sa mort. »

paras.summary: Dorian says Sibyl died because of him. Lord Henry says she took the poison herself and that Dorian did not know she would.

s.t: "She was a girl who lived in a theatre, and she thought that everything was a play," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « C’était une jeune fille qui vivait au théâtre, et pour elle tout n’était que comédie, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "She ended her life as a girl ends it in a play, and men will remember her as beautiful."
s.fr: « Elle a mis fin à ses jours comme meurent les jeunes filles au théâtre, et l’on gardera d’elle le souvenir de sa beauté. »

s.t: "You would have been tired of her in a year, and she would have been unhappy."
s.fr: « Au bout d’un an, vous vous seriez lassé d’elle, et elle aurait été malheureuse. »

s.t: "It is better this way, Dorian, and you must not be sad."
s.fr: « Mieux vaut qu’il en soit ainsi, Dorian, et vous ne devez pas être triste. »

s.t: "You loved her because she was a great actress, and that is why you must think of her as Juliet."
s.fr: « Vous l’aimiez parce qu’elle était une grande actrice, et voilà pourquoi vous devez penser à elle comme à Juliette. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry says Sibyl thought everything was a play and ended her life as a girl does in one, and that she will be remembered as beautiful. He says Dorian would have grown tired of her and should think of her as Juliet.

s.t: "You are right, Harry," Dorian said, and he was silent for a time.
s.fr: « Vous avez raison, Harry, » dit Dorian, et il se tut un moment.

s.t: "I was in love with her, and now she is dead, and I am not as sad as I ought to be."
s.fr: « J’étais amoureux d’elle, maintenant elle est morte, et je ne suis pas aussi triste que je le devrais. »

s.t: "I do not know why, and it is strange."
s.fr: « Je ne sais pas pourquoi, et c’est étrange. »

s.t: "You are a strange man," Lord Henry said, "and I like you for it."
s.fr: « Vous êtes un homme étrange, dit lord Henry, et c’est pour cela que je vous aime bien. »

paras.summary: Dorian agrees and says he is not as sad as he ought to be and does not know why. Lord Henry calls him strange and says he likes him for it.

s.t: "Come with me to the opera tonight," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Venez avec moi à l’opéra ce soir, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "I will come," Dorian said, and he looked at the screen in front of the picture.
s.fr: « Je viendrai, » dit Dorian, et il regarda le paravent qui cachait le portrait.

s.t: "I must hide that picture, Harry, for I do not want anyone to see it."
s.fr: « Il faut que je cache ce portrait, Harry, car je ne veux pas que quiconque le voie. »

s.t: "It has changed, and it shows what I am."
s.fr: « Il a changé, et il montre ce que je suis. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry asks Dorian to come to the opera, and Dorian agrees. Dorian says he must hide the picture because it has changed and shows what he is.

s.t: "You are tired, Dorian, and a picture cannot change," Lord Henry said.
s.fr: « Vous êtes fatigué, Dorian, et un portrait ne peut pas changer, » dit lord Henry.

s.t: "It has changed, Harry, and I know that it has," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Il a changé, Harry, et je le sais, » dit Dorian.

s.t: Lord Henry laughed and did not believe him.
s.fr: Lord Henry rit et ne le crut pas.

s.t: He went out of the room, and Dorian was alone with the screen.
s.fr: Il sortit de la pièce, et Dorian resta seul face au paravent.

s.t: Dorian looked at the screen for a long time, and then he called his servant.
s.fr: Dorian contempla longuement le paravent, puis il appela son domestique.

s.t: He wanted to find a place for the picture where no one would see it.
s.fr: Il voulait trouver pour le portrait un endroit où personne ne le verrait.

paras.summary: Lord Henry says a picture cannot change and laughs, then leaves. Dorian calls his servant, for he wants to find a hidden place for the picture.

s.t: That day Basil came to the house, and Dorian met him in the hall.
s.fr: Ce jour-là, Basil vint à la maison, et Dorian le reçut dans le vestibule.

s.t: "I am sorry about Sibyl, Dorian," Basil said.
s.fr: « Je suis navré pour Sibyl, Dorian, » dit Basil.

s.t: "I have come to ask you for the picture."
s.fr: « Je suis venu vous demander le portrait. »

s.t: "I want to send it to the gallery this year."
s.fr: « Je voudrais l’exposer cette année. »

paras.summary: That day Basil comes to Dorian's house, says he is sorry about Sibyl, and asks for the picture for the gallery.

s.t: "No, you must not send it," Dorian said, and his face grew cold.
s.fr: « Non, vous ne l’exposerez pas, » dit Dorian, et son visage se glaça.

s.t: "You gave it to me, and I will not show it to anyone."
s.fr: « Vous me l’avez donné, et je ne le montrerai à personne. »

s.t: "Why will you not show it?" Basil asked.
s.fr: « Pourquoi ne voulez-vous pas le montrer ? » demanda Basil.

s.t: "I will tell you one day," Dorian said, "but you must never ask me again."
s.fr: « Je vous le dirai un jour, dit Dorian, mais vous ne devez plus jamais me le demander. »

paras.summary: Dorian refuses and says he will not show the picture to anyone, that he may tell Basil why one day, and that Basil must never ask again.

s.t: Basil looked at him for a long time and said, "I will not ask again."
s.fr: Basil le regarda longuement et dit : « Je ne vous le demanderai plus. »

s.t: "You look tired, Dorian, and you must not lose your friends."
s.fr: « Vous avez l’air fatigué, Dorian, et il ne faut pas perdre vos amis. »

s.t: "I do not want to lose you," Basil said.
s.fr: « Je ne veux pas vous perdre, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You will not lose me," Dorian said, and he smiled.
s.fr: « Vous ne me perdrez pas, » dit Dorian en souriant.

s.t: Basil went away, and Dorian stood in the hall and did not move.
s.fr: Basil s’en alla, et Dorian resta immobile dans le vestibule.

paras.summary: Basil says he will not ask again and does not want to lose Dorian. Dorian smiles and says he will not, and Basil leaves.

s.t: Dorian went up to the old room at the top of the house, where he had been a boy.
s.fr: Dorian monta jusqu’à la vieille chambre, tout en haut de la maison, où il avait passé son enfance.

s.t: The room was empty, and the door had a lock.
s.fr: La pièce était vide, et la porte fermait à clé.

s.t: He remembered the boy who had lived in that room, and the boy was young and good.
s.fr: Il se souvint du garçon qui avait vécu dans cette pièce, et ce garçon était jeune et bon.

s.t: Dorian called Victor and two men, and he told them that they must not look at the picture.
s.fr: Dorian fit venir Victor et deux hommes, et il leur ordonna de ne pas regarder le portrait.

s.t: They carried it up the stairs with a cloth over it, and Dorian walked behind them.
s.fr: Ils le montèrent par l’escalier, recouvert d’une étoffe, et Dorian les suivait.

paras.summary: Dorian goes up to the old room where he was a boy and remembers the young, good boy he was. Victor and two men carry the covered picture up the stairs.

s.t: Dorian put the picture on the floor and sent the men away.
s.fr: Dorian posa le portrait par terre et congédia les hommes.

s.t: He locked the door, and he put the key in his pocket.
s.fr: Il ferma la porte à double tour et mit la clé dans sa poche.

s.t: He told himself that no one would ever see the picture.
s.fr: Il se dit que personne ne verrait jamais le portrait.

s.t: He took the letter that he had written to Sibyl and tore it up.
s.fr: Il prit la lettre qu’il avait écrite à Sibyl et la déchira.

s.t: He did not want to think about Sibyl, and he did not want to think about the picture.
s.fr: Il ne voulait plus penser à Sibyl, ni au portrait.

s.t: That night he went to the opera with Lord Henry.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, il alla à l’opéra avec lord Henry.

paras.summary: Dorian sends the men away, locks the door, and keeps the key, telling himself no one will see the picture. He tears up his letter to Sibyl and, not wanting to think about her or the picture, goes to the opera with Lord Henry.

s.t: A few days later Lord Henry sent Dorian a book with a yellow cover.
s.fr: Quelques jours plus tard, lord Henry envoya à Dorian un livre à couverture jaune.

s.t: Dorian read it all night, and in the morning he could not put it down.
s.fr: Dorian le lut toute la nuit, et au matin il ne pouvait toujours pas le lâcher.

s.t: It was a book about a young man who wanted every pleasure, and Dorian thought that the young man was himself.
s.fr: C’était l’histoire d’un jeune homme avide de tous les plaisirs, et Dorian crut se reconnaître en lui.

s.t: He read it again and again, and for years he thought about it.
s.fr: Il le relut maintes et maintes fois, et il y pensa pendant des années.

s.t: "Do you like the book, Dorian?" Lord Henry asked.
s.fr: « Ce livre vous plaît-il, Dorian ? » demanda lord Henry.

s.t: "It is the best book that I have ever read, and I think that it was written about me," Dorian said.
s.fr: « C’est le plus beau livre que j’aie jamais lu, et je crois qu’il a été écrit sur moi, » dit Dorian.

s.t: Lord Henry laughed and said, "It was written about every young man who is not afraid to live."
s.fr: Lord Henry rit et répondit : « Il a été écrit sur tous les jeunes gens qui n’ont pas peur de vivre. »

paras.summary: Lord Henry sends Dorian a book with a yellow cover, about a young man who wanted every pleasure. Dorian reads it all night and thinks it is about himself, and Lord Henry says it is about every young man who is not afraid to live.

s.t: Dorian lived as Lord Henry had said, and he did what he wanted to do.
s.fr: Dorian vécut comme lord Henry le lui avait conseillé, et il fit tout ce qui lui plaisait.

s.t: He gave dinners, and he went to strange places, and he knew many people.
s.fr: Il donnait des dîners, fréquentait des lieux étranges et connaissait beaucoup de monde.

s.t: Young men went with him, and they lost their money and their good names.
s.fr: Des jeunes gens le suivaient, et ils y perdaient leur argent et leur bon renom.

s.t: People said bad things about Dorian, and they said that he was cruel.
s.fr: On disait du mal de Dorian, et on le disait cruel.

s.t: But they looked at his young face and did not believe it.
s.fr: Mais on regardait son jeune visage, et on n’y croyait pas.

s.t: Many men still came to his house, for he was rich and beautiful.
s.fr: Bien des gens venaient encore chez lui, car il était riche et beau.

paras.summary: Dorian lives as Lord Henry taught him. Young men who go with him lose their money and good names, and people call him cruel, but his young face makes them doubt it, and many still come to his house.

s.t: Many years went by, and Dorian did not grow old.
s.fr: De longues années passèrent, et Dorian ne vieillissait pas.

s.t: He went up to the locked room and took the cloth from the picture.
s.fr: Il monta dans la pièce fermée à clé et retira l’étoffe qui couvrait le portrait.

s.t: The face in the picture was old now, and the mouth was cruel, and the eyes were hard.
s.fr: Le visage du portrait avait vieilli, la bouche était cruelle, et les yeux étaient durs.

s.t: He looked at his own face in a mirror, and it was young and beautiful.
s.fr: Il regarda son propre visage dans un miroir, et il était jeune et beau.

paras.summary: Many years go by, and Dorian does not grow old. In the locked room the picture shows an old face with a cruel mouth, while his own face in the mirror is young.

s.t: He looked at the picture again, and he laughed.
s.fr: Il regarda de nouveau le portrait, et il éclata de rire.

s.t: He thought of Sibyl sometimes, but he did not feel sad, and he did not think of her for long.
s.fr: Il lui arrivait de penser à Sibyl, mais sans tristesse, et jamais bien longtemps.

s.t: Basil came to the house often, and he was sad when men spoke against Dorian.
s.fr: Basil venait souvent chez lui, et il s’attristait quand on disait du mal de Dorian.

s.t: He did not believe them, and he had not asked about the picture again.
s.fr: Il ne les croyait pas, et il n’avait plus jamais posé de question sur le portrait.

paras.summary: Dorian laughs at the picture and does not feel sad when he thinks of Sibyl. Basil, who comes often, does not believe what men say and never asks about the picture.

s.t: Many years after the night of the opera, Dorian walked home in the cold on his birthday.
s.fr: Bien des années après ce soir d’opéra, le jour de son anniversaire, Dorian rentrait chez lui à pied dans le froid.

s.t: He was 38 years old, but he still had the face of a young man.
s.fr: Il avait trente-huit ans, mais il gardait toujours le visage d’un jeune homme.

s.t: The night was dark, and no one else was in the street.
s.fr: La nuit était noire, et il n’y avait personne d’autre dans la rue.

s.t: Basil came out of the fog and said, "Dorian, I want to speak to you."
s.fr: Basil surgit du brouillard et dit : « Dorian, je voudrais vous parler. »

s.t: "I am going to Paris tonight, but I must speak to you first."
s.fr: « Je pars pour Paris ce soir, mais il faut d’abord que je vous parle. »

paras.summary: Many years later, on his birthday, Dorian walks home in the cold with the face of a young man. Basil comes out of the fog and says he must speak to him before he goes to Paris.

s.t: They went into the house, and Basil sat down in the room.
s.fr: Ils entrèrent dans la maison, et Basil s’assit dans le salon.

s.t: "Dorian, men say bad things about you," Basil said.
s.fr: « Dorian, on raconte de vilaines choses sur vous, » dit Basil.

s.t: "A young man who was your friend killed himself, and other young men lost their good names."
s.fr: « Un jeune homme qui était votre ami s’est donné la mort, et d’autres jeunes gens ont perdu leur bon renom. »

s.t: "The mothers in London do not want their boys to meet you."
s.fr: « À Londres, les mères ne veulent pas que leurs fils vous fréquentent. »

s.t: "Men say that you go to bad places at night, and that you come home in the morning."
s.fr: « On dit que vous hantez de mauvais lieux la nuit, et que vous ne rentrez qu’au matin. »

paras.summary: They go into the house, where Basil says men say bad things about Dorian. A young man who was his friend killed himself, other young men lost their good names, and mothers do not want their boys to meet him.

s.t: "Do not tell me about other men's lives," Dorian said, "for you do not know my life."
s.fr: « Ne me parlez pas de la vie des autres, dit Dorian, car vous ne connaissez pas la mienne. »

s.t: "I know what you were," Basil said.
s.fr: « Je sais ce que vous étiez, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You were the best young man in London, and you were my best friend."
s.fr: « Vous étiez le meilleur des jeunes gens de Londres, et vous étiez mon meilleur ami. »

s.t: "Now men will not speak to you, and I do not know why."
s.fr: « Aujourd’hui, les gens refusent de vous adresser la parole, et je ne sais pas pourquoi. »

s.t: "I do not believe the things that men say, for I look at your face, and it is young and good."
s.fr: « Je ne crois pas ce que l’on raconte, car je regarde votre visage, et j’y vois la jeunesse et la bonté. »

paras.summary: Dorian says Basil does not know his life. Basil says Dorian was the best young man in London and his best friend, and that men now will not speak to him. He does not believe them when he looks at Dorian's face.

s.t: "Tell me that these things are not true, Dorian."
s.fr: « Dites-moi que tout cela n’est pas vrai, Dorian. »

s.t: "I will not tell you that," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Je ne vous dirai pas cela, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "I cannot know your life if I do not see your soul."
s.fr: « Pour connaître votre vie, il faudrait que je voie votre âme. »

s.t: Dorian's face was strange, and then it grew hard.
s.fr: Le visage de Dorian prit un air étrange, puis se durcit.

paras.summary: Basil asks Dorian to deny the stories, but Dorian will not, and Basil says he cannot know Dorian's life without seeing his soul.

s.t: "You shall see my soul, Basil," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Vous la verrez, mon âme, Basil, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "You shall see it with your own eyes, and you shall not go to Paris until you have seen it."
s.fr: « Vous la verrez de vos propres yeux, et vous ne partirez pas pour Paris avant de l’avoir vue. »

s.t: "Come with me, and I will show you the thing that you asked for."
s.fr: « Venez avec moi, et je vous montrerai ce que vous m’avez demandé. »

s.t: "I am not afraid of what I will see," Basil said.
s.fr: « Je n’ai pas peur de ce que je vais voir, » dit Basil.

s.t: "You are afraid," Dorian said, "but you will come."
s.fr: « Vous avez peur, dit Dorian, mais vous viendrez. »

paras.summary: Dorian says Basil shall see his soul and tells him to come, and Basil says he is not afraid.

s.t: Dorian took a lamp and went up the stairs with Basil to the room at the top of the house.
s.fr: Dorian prit une lampe et monta l’escalier avec Basil jusqu’à la pièce tout en haut de la maison.

s.t: He took the key from his pocket and opened the door.
s.fr: Il tira la clé de sa poche et ouvrit la porte.

s.t: He took the cloth from the picture and said, "Look at it, Basil."
s.fr: Il retira l’étoffe qui couvrait le portrait et dit : « Regardez, Basil. »

s.t: Basil looked at the picture, and then he cried out.
s.fr: Basil regarda le portrait, puis il poussa un cri.

s.t: The face in the picture was old, and the mouth was cruel, and the eyes were hard.
s.fr: Le visage du portrait était vieux, la bouche cruelle, et les yeux durs.

paras.summary: Dorian takes Basil up to the locked room, opens it with his key, and takes the cloth off the picture. Basil looks and cries out at the old face with the cruel mouth and hard eyes.

s.t: "It is my picture," Basil said, and his voice was low.
s.fr: « C’est mon portrait, » dit Basil d’une voix sourde.

s.t: "I painted it, and my name is on it."
s.fr: « C’est moi qui l’ai peint, et il porte ma signature. »

s.t: "What has been done to it?"
s.fr: « Qu’a-t-on fait à ce portrait ? »

s.t: "I made a wish in your studio, Basil, and the wish came true," Dorian said.
s.fr: « J’ai formé un vœu dans votre atelier, Basil, et ce vœu a été exaucé, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "You painted my face, and you told me that it was beautiful."
s.fr: « Vous avez peint mon visage, et vous m’avez dit qu’il était beau. »

s.t: "I said that the picture could be old in my place."
s.fr: « J’ai dit que le portrait pourrait vieillir à ma place. »

paras.summary: Basil recognizes the picture as his own and asks what has been done to it. Dorian says he made a wish in the studio, that the picture could be old in his place, and that it came true.

s.t: "Now you see what I am, and the picture shows it."
s.fr: « Maintenant vous voyez ce que je suis, et le portrait le montre. »

s.t: "Pray, Dorian," Basil said, "and ask to be forgiven."
s.fr: « Priez, Dorian, dit Basil, et demandez pardon. »

s.t: "It is too late," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Il est trop tard, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "It is never too late," Basil said.
s.fr: « Il n’est jamais trop tard, » dit Basil.

s.t: "Go down on your knees and pray."
s.fr: « Mettez-vous à genoux et priez. »

s.t: Dorian looked at Basil, and he had a great hate for him.
s.fr: Dorian regarda Basil, et il éprouva pour lui une haine immense.

paras.summary: Dorian says the picture shows what he is. Basil tells him to pray, but Dorian says it is too late and looks at Basil with hate.

s.t: Dorian saw a knife on the table, and he took it in his hand.
s.fr: Dorian aperçut un couteau sur la table et s’en saisit.

s.t: He walked behind Basil, and he stabbed him in the neck.
s.fr: Il passa derrière Basil et lui planta la lame dans le cou.

s.t: Basil cried out once, and then he fell on the floor and did not move.
s.fr: Basil poussa un cri, un seul, puis il s’écroula sur le plancher et ne bougea plus.

s.t: Dorian stabbed him again and again, and then he stood still and listened, but no one came.
s.fr: Dorian le frappa encore et encore, puis il s’immobilisa et tendit l’oreille, mais personne ne vint.

paras.summary: Dorian takes a knife, walks behind Basil, and stabs him in the neck. Basil falls and does not move, and Dorian stabs him again and again, then listens, but no one comes.

s.t: Dorian looked at the dead man, and he did not feel afraid.
s.fr: Dorian regarda le mort, et il n’éprouva aucune peur.

s.t: He looked at his hands, and they were young and beautiful.
s.fr: Il regarda ses mains, et elles étaient jeunes et belles.

s.t: He put the cloth on the picture and locked the door.
s.fr: Il remit l’étoffe sur le portrait et ferma la porte à clé.

s.t: He took the lamp and went down the stairs, and he sat in the room and thought.
s.fr: Il prit la lampe, descendit l’escalier, puis s’assit dans le salon pour réfléchir.

s.t: He must hide the dead man before the morning.
s.fr: Il lui fallait cacher le mort avant le matin.

paras.summary: Dorian is not afraid, and his hands are young and beautiful. He covers the picture, locks the door, and goes down to think about how to hide the dead man.

s.t: Dorian sat in the room and thought, and at last he took a pen and wrote a letter.
s.fr: Dorian resta assis à réfléchir, et il prit enfin une plume pour écrire une lettre.

s.t: The letter was to Alan Campbell, who had once been his friend.
s.fr: La lettre était destinée à Alan Campbell, qui avait été jadis son ami.

s.t: Alan knew about chemistry, and he had not spoken to Dorian for years.
s.fr: Alan s’y connaissait en chimie, et il n’avait pas adressé la parole à Dorian depuis des années.

s.t: Dorian sent the letter by Victor and told him to bring Alan back at once.
s.fr: Dorian fit porter la lettre par Victor en lui ordonnant de ramener Alan sur-le-champ.

paras.summary: Dorian writes to Alan Campbell, a former friend who knows chemistry and has not spoken to him for years. He sends the letter by Victor and tells him to bring Alan back at once.

s.t: Alan came at two in the morning, and his face was white and hard.
s.fr: Alan arriva à deux heures du matin, le visage blême et dur.

s.t: "I came because you asked, Dorian, but I do not want to see you," Alan said.
s.fr: « Je suis venu parce que vous me l’avez demandé, Dorian, mais je ne tiens pas à vous voir, » dit Alan.

s.t: "There is a dead man in the room at the top of the house," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Il y a un mort dans la pièce tout en haut de la maison, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "You must destroy the body, so that no one can find it."
s.fr: « Vous devez faire disparaître le corps, pour que personne ne puisse le retrouver. »

paras.summary: Alan comes at two in the morning and says he does not want to see Dorian. Dorian says a dead man lies at the top of the house and Alan must destroy the body.

s.t: "Who is the man?" Alan asked.
s.fr: « Qui est cet homme ? » demanda Alan.

s.t: "It is Basil Hallward," Dorian said.
s.fr: « C’est Basil Hallward, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "Basil!" Alan cried.
s.fr: « Basil ! » s’écria Alan.

s.t: "Did you kill him?"
s.fr: « Vous l’avez tué ? »

s.t: "I did," Dorian said, "and no one must know it."
s.fr: « Oui, dit Dorian, et personne ne doit le savoir. »

s.t: "You know what to do, for you know chemistry, and you can do it in one night."
s.fr: « Vous savez ce qu’il faut faire, car vous connaissez la chimie, et une nuit vous suffira. »

paras.summary: Alan asks who the man is, and Dorian says it is Basil Hallward and that he killed him. Dorian says Alan can do it in one night.

s.t: "I will not do it," Alan said.
s.fr: « Je ne le ferai pas, » dit Alan.

s.t: "You have killed a man, and I will not help you."
s.fr: « Vous avez tué un homme, et je ne vous aiderai pas. »

s.t: "I do not ask you to kill," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Je ne vous demande pas de tuer, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "I ask you to do a thing that only you can do."
s.fr: « Je vous demande de faire une chose que vous seul pouvez faire. »

s.t: Dorian wrote a few words on a paper and gave it to Alan.
s.fr: Dorian griffonna quelques mots sur un bout de papier et le tendit à Alan.

paras.summary: Alan refuses to help a man who has killed. Dorian says only Alan can do it and gives him a paper with a few words on it.

s.t: Alan read the paper, and his face grew whiter still.
s.fr: Alan lut le papier, et son visage devint plus blême encore.

s.t: The paper told a secret of his life, and he did not want anyone to know it.
s.fr: Le papier révélait un secret de sa vie, et il ne voulait pas que quiconque l’apprenne.

s.t: "I will send this paper to your friends if you do not help me," Dorian said.
s.fr: « J’enverrai ce papier à vos amis si vous ne m’aidez pas, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "You are a bad man," Alan said, "but I will do it."
s.fr: « Vous êtes ignoble, dit Alan, mais je le ferai. »

paras.summary: Alan reads a paper that tells a secret of his life. Dorian says he will send it to Alan's friends unless Alan helps, and Alan agrees.

s.t: Alan wrote a list of the things that he needed, and Dorian gave it to Victor.
s.fr: Alan dressa la liste de ce dont il avait besoin, et Dorian la remit à Victor.

s.t: "Bring them here, and bring them quickly," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Rapportez tout cela ici, et faites vite, » dit Dorian.

s.t: At 4 in the morning Victor came back, and Alan carried the things up the stairs.
s.fr: À quatre heures du matin, Victor revint, et Alan monta le tout par l’escalier.

s.t: Dorian waited in the room below, and he did not move for a long time.
s.fr: Dorian attendit en bas, et il resta longtemps sans bouger.

paras.summary: Alan lists what he needs, and Victor brings it at 4 in the morning. Alan goes upstairs while Dorian waits below.

s.t: At 7 in the morning Alan came down the stairs, and his face was white and tired.
s.fr: À sept heures du matin, Alan redescendit l’escalier, le visage blême et fatigué.

s.t: "It is finished," Alan said, "and there is nothing left in the room."
s.fr: « C’est fini, dit Alan, et il ne reste plus rien dans la pièce. »

s.t: "You have saved me, Alan," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Vous m’avez sauvé, Alan, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "I wish that I had not," Alan said.
s.fr: « J’aurais préféré ne pas le faire, » dit Alan.

s.t: "I do not want to see you again, Dorian, and I do not want to hear your name."
s.fr: « Je ne veux plus vous revoir, Dorian, ni entendre prononcer votre nom. »

paras.summary: Alan comes down, white and tired, and says there is nothing left in the room. Dorian thanks him, but Alan says he wishes he had not and never wants to see Dorian again.

s.t: Alan went out of the house, and Dorian stood in the hall and did not move.
s.fr: Alan quitta la maison, et Dorian resta immobile dans le vestibule.

s.t: After a time he went up to the room and looked at the picture, and it was the same.
s.fr: Au bout d’un moment, il monta dans la pièce et regarda le portrait, qui n’avait pas changé.

s.t: He washed his hands for a long time, and he changed his clothes.
s.fr: Il se lava longuement les mains, et il changea de vêtements.

s.t: That evening he put on his best clothes again, and he went to dinner at the house of Lady Narborough.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, il revêtit de nouveau ses plus beaux habits et alla dîner chez lady Narborough.

paras.summary: Alan leaves. Dorian looks at the picture, which is the same, washes his hands, and changes his clothes. That evening he goes to dinner at Lady Narborough's house.

s.t: Dorian laughed and talked with everyone at the table, and no one saw that anything was wrong.
s.fr: Dorian riait et bavardait avec tous les convives, et personne ne remarqua que quelque chose n’allait pas.

s.t: Lady Narborough said that he was the best young man in London, and he smiled.
s.fr: Lady Narborough déclara qu’il était le meilleur des jeunes gens de Londres, et il sourit.

s.t: He ate little, and he did not look at the door.
s.fr: Il mangea peu, et il ne regarda pas la porte.

s.t: "Why are you so quiet, Dorian?" Lady Narborough asked.
s.fr: « Pourquoi êtes-vous si silencieux, Dorian ? » demanda lady Narborough.

s.t: "I am tired, for I did not sleep last night," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Je suis fatigué, car je n’ai pas dormi de la nuit, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "I think that you are in love," she said, and she laughed.
s.fr: « Je crois que vous êtes amoureux, » dit-elle en riant.

paras.summary: Dorian laughs and talks at the table, and Lady Narborough says he is the best young man in London. He eats little and says he is tired because he did not sleep, and she says he must be in love.

s.t: After dinner Lord Henry sat by him and said, "Basil has gone to Paris, and he did not say goodbye."
s.fr: Après le dîner, lord Henry vint s’asseoir auprès de lui et dit : « Basil est parti pour Paris sans dire au revoir. »

s.t: "He said that he was going," Dorian said, "and he left in a hurry."
s.fr: « Il m’avait dit qu’il partait, répondit Dorian, et il est parti en hâte. »

s.t: "That is strange," Lord Henry said, "for Basil never leaves without saying goodbye."
s.fr: « Voilà qui est étrange, dit lord Henry, car Basil ne part jamais sans dire au revoir. »

s.t: "He is a strange man," Dorian said, "and he may have changed his mind."
s.fr: « C’est un homme étrange, dit Dorian, et il aura peut-être changé d’avis. »

s.t: Lord Henry looked at Dorian for a long time and said nothing more.
s.fr: Lord Henry regarda longuement Dorian et n’ajouta rien.

s.t: Dorian left the house early, and he could not stop thinking about the room at the top of his own house.
s.fr: Dorian partit de bonne heure, et il ne pouvait s’empêcher de penser à la pièce tout en haut de sa propre maison.

paras.summary: Lord Henry says Basil has gone to Paris without saying goodbye. Dorian says he left in a hurry, and Lord Henry says it is strange. Lord Henry looks at him and says no more, and Dorian leaves early.

s.t: That night Dorian could not stay in his house, and he took a cab to a poor part of London by the river.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, Dorian ne put rester chez lui, et il prit un fiacre pour un quartier pauvre de Londres, au bord du fleuve.

s.t: "Where do you want to go?" the driver asked.
s.fr: « Où voulez-vous aller ? » demanda le cocher.

s.t: "Drive on until I tell you to stop," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Roulez jusqu’à ce que je vous dise de vous arrêter, » dit Dorian.

s.t: The cab stopped in front of a dirty house, and Dorian went in and sat down.
s.fr: Le fiacre s’arrêta devant une maison crasseuse, et Dorian entra et s’assit.

s.t: The room was dark, and men lay on the floor with pipes in their mouths.
s.fr: La salle était sombre, et des hommes gisaient sur le sol, la pipe à la bouche.

paras.summary: That night Dorian takes a cab to a poor part of London by the river and finally goes into a dirty, dark house where men lie on the floor with pipes.

s.t: "Give me a pipe," Dorian said to the man of the house.
s.fr: « Donnez-moi une pipe, » dit Dorian au maître des lieux.

s.t: "It will cost you money," the man said.
s.fr: « Il faudra payer, » dit l’homme.

s.t: "I have money," Dorian said, and he took a pipe and smoked it too.
s.fr: « J’ai de l’argent, » dit Dorian, et il prit une pipe qu’il fuma à son tour.

s.t: He wanted to forget the room at the top of his house, and he wanted to forget the picture.
s.fr: Il voulait oublier la pièce tout en haut de sa maison, et il voulait oublier le portrait.

s.t: A young man named Adrian Singleton lay by him and looked at him with hard eyes.
s.fr: Un jeune homme du nom d’Adrian Singleton, étendu près de lui, le fixait d’un regard dur.

s.t: "You are the man who spoiled my life," Adrian said, "and I do not want to speak to you."
s.fr: « C’est vous qui avez gâché ma vie, dit Adrian, et je ne veux pas vous parler. »

s.t: Dorian stood up and went out of the room and into the street.
s.fr: Dorian se leva, quitta la salle et sortit dans la rue.

paras.summary: Dorian smokes opium to forget the picture. A young man named Adrian Singleton says Dorian spoiled his life, and Dorian leaves.

s.t: A woman ran after him, and her face was hard.
s.fr: Une femme courut après lui, le visage dur.

s.t: "There is the Prince!" the woman cried.
s.fr: « Voilà le Prince Charmant ! » cria la femme.

s.t: "You are the man who gave his soul to the devil, and I hate you!"
s.fr: « Tu es celui qui a vendu son âme au diable, et je te hais ! »

s.t: Her voice was loud, and men in the street turned to look.
s.fr: Elle criait fort, et dans la rue des passants se retournèrent.

s.t: Dorian gave her money and walked on quickly.
s.fr: Dorian lui donna de l’argent et pressa le pas.

paras.summary: A hard-faced woman runs after Dorian, crying that he is the Prince and has given his soul to the devil. He gives her money and walks on.

s.t: A sailor was sitting in the dark by the door, and he heard the woman cry out.
s.fr: Un marin était assis dans l’ombre, près de la porte, et il entendit la femme crier.

s.t: He stood up, and his eyes were on Dorian, and his hand was in his pocket.
s.fr: Il se leva, les yeux fixés sur Dorian, la main dans la poche.

s.t: The sailor was James Vane, and he had come back from Australia.
s.fr: Ce marin, c’était James Vane, qui revenait d’Australie.

s.t: For years he had looked for the man who spoiled his sister, and he knew only that she had called him the Prince.
s.fr: Depuis des années, il cherchait l’homme qui avait perdu sa sœur, et il savait seulement qu’elle l’appelait le Prince Charmant.

s.t: He went after Dorian into the street, and Dorian did not see him.
s.fr: Il suivit Dorian dans la rue, et Dorian ne le vit pas.

paras.summary: A sailor by the door hears the woman and stands up. He is James Vane, home from Australia, who has looked for years for the man his sister called the Prince, and he follows Dorian unseen.

s.t: Dorian walked to the river, and a hand took him by the neck from behind.
s.fr: Dorian marcha jusqu’au fleuve, et une main le saisit par derrière, à la gorge.

s.t: He felt the end of a gun, and a voice said, "Do not move, for I will kill you if you do."
s.fr: Il sentit le canon d’un revolver, et une voix dit : « Pas un geste, ou je te tue. »

s.t: "Who are you?" Dorian asked, and his voice was low.
s.fr: « Qui êtes-vous ? » demanda Dorian d’une voix sourde.

s.t: "I am James Vane, and you are the man that my sister called the Prince," the voice said.
s.fr: « Je suis James Vane, et tu es l’homme que ma sœur appelait le Prince Charmant, » dit la voix.

s.t: "Pray, for you will die tonight."
s.fr: « Fais ta prière, car tu vas mourir cette nuit. »

paras.summary: A hand takes Dorian by the neck from behind, and a gun touches him. The voice says it is James Vane, that Dorian is the man his sister called the Prince, and that he will die tonight.

s.t: "I do not know any Sibyl Vane," Dorian said.
s.fr: « Je ne connais aucune Sibyl Vane, » dit Dorian.

s.t: "She has been dead for 18 years, and I was only a boy then."
s.fr: « Elle est morte depuis dix-huit ans, et je n’étais alors qu’un enfant. »

s.t: "Tell me your name," James said.
s.fr: « Dis-moi ton nom, » dit James.

s.t: "My name is Dorian Gray, and no one has ever called me the Prince."
s.fr: « Je m’appelle Dorian Gray, et personne ne m’a jamais appelé le Prince Charmant. »
